agent.problem: Several choice questions rely on context that is no longer on screen. In stop 1, cards 5, 10 and 13 use 'they' or 'their' without identifying the Gentiles or believers, and card 7 refers to 'this way of living' without identifying the Gentiles' way of life. In stop 2, cards 14 and 17 likewise use 'they' without naming Paul's audience. Each question should supply its own antecedents and context.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: "Sealed for a day" changes Ephesians 4:30's "sealed for the day of redemption." The verse names the day of redemption; it does not describe a one-day duration. The joke's setup should preserve that meaning.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

agent.problem: This story card is only Papa Dorin's personal joke about not keeping a drawer of grudges. It does not tell any part of Ephesians 4:32, the verse it cites, or carry the passage forward; the kindness, tenderheartedness and Christ-patterned forgiveness appear only in the preceding choice card.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.
